Class ConstructalFlowArchitectureEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.ConstructalFlowArchitectureEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class ConstructalFlowArchitectureEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Universal Constructal Law of Flow Architecture & Locomotion Allometry Engine.

Formalizes Adrian Bejan's Constructal Law of thermodynamic flow systems (Bejan 1996, 2000; Bejan & Marden 2006, Journal of Experimental Biology; Bejan 2016, The Physics of Life):

"For a finite-size flow system to persist in time (to live), its configuration must evolve in such a way that it provides easier and easier access to the currents that flow through it."

Governs non-human and planetary physical phenomena across three domains:

  1. Universal Animal Locomotion Velocity (runners, flyers, swimmers): Balances work against gravitational potential against aerodynamic/hydrodynamic drag: \[ V_{\text{opt}}(M) = V_0 \cdot M_{\text{body}}^{1/6}, \qquad f_{\text{stride}}(M) = f_0 \cdot M_{\text{body}}^{-1/6} \] Valid across insects, fish, reptiles, birds, mammals, and hominins spanning 8 orders of mass magnitude.
  2. Murray's Law of Vascular & Plant Xylem Branching: Minimizes hydraulic pumping power dissipation in dendritic vascular networks: \[ d_{\text{parent}}^3 = \sum_{i=1}^n d_{\text{daughter}, i}^3 \]
  3. Hack's Law of River Catchment Scaling: Drainage stream length scales with catchment basin area as: \[ L_{\text{stream}} = c_{\text{hack}} \cdot A_{\text{basin}}^{0.57} \]
